decision: The demo proves three local-first loops: job discovery with distance, independently sourced profile/resume updates, and minimal daily/weekly work reports. Advanced matching and application tracking are deferred.
why: This preserves the full product intent while keeping the first implementation demonstrable.

decision: Store and use the exact home address only locally; use rotating nearby landmarks for external queries; obtain public job-location coordinates externally and compute final straight-line distance to the exact local coordinate on-device.
why: The user requires location-aware job discovery without disclosing the exact residence externally.

decision: Job discovery cannot directly modify the personal profile or resume; profile/resume updates use only user-imported or confirmed evidence, and work-report promotion requires confirmation.
why: The user explicitly requires resume updating and job discovery to remain isolated.

decision: Scheduled public-data reads and updates to pre-authorized local records are allowed; applications, messages, uploads, account authorization, and all other external writes require explicit user confirmation.
why: This is the agreed autonomy boundary for the demo.

decision: Root goal.md is the highest-priority product and boundary contract; goal/ contains subordinate architecture, research, plan, decisions, and append-only implementation records. Technical documents cannot silently change product intent.
why: The user requires a goal directory that remains aligned with the confirmed intent while becoming implementation-ready.

decision: Use the pinned and trimmed FastAPI full-stack template as the application base, LangGraph OSS as local orchestration, React/TypeScript for the dashboard, PostgreSQL for business data and checkpoints, APScheduler in a separate worker, and Docker Compose for local runtime.
why: This balances local-first constraints, implementation maturity, portfolio recognition, and a manageable demo scope.

decision: Remote GPT or other AI models are injected through a project-owned ModelProvider gateway. Local code performs parsing, minimization, policy checks, schema validation, and persistence; exact address, exact home coordinates, secrets, unrelated files, and the full database are blocked from outbound requests.
why: The user wants remote AI capability combined with a local agent without sacrificing the agreed privacy boundary.

decision: Clone the FastAPI template into a unique temporary directory, inspect its license and instructions, record a pinned commit, and selectively import declared application paths without copying upstream Git history or agent instructions. Use JobSpy, LangGraph, MarkItDown, and JSON Resume through pinned dependencies or schemas.
why: This preserves provenance and mature engineering structure while keeping MiniWorld's goal and Git history authoritative.

decision: Execute the implementation as a repository-wide bootstrap with explicit commit boundaries: goal baseline, pinned upstream import, local single-user reduction, feature loops, verification, and documentation. Do not push publicly or use real personal data/secrets while the user is away.
why: The user asked for autonomous progress, Git management, a runnable demo, tests, README updates, and accumulated decisions without intent drift.

decision: Run LangGraph OSS entirely in the local API/worker environment with PostgreSQL checkpoints; LangGraph Cloud and LangSmith are optional future services, not Demo dependencies.
why: The user explicitly confirmed the local LangGraph route and wants a technically current, job-market-recognizable project without weakening local-first constraints.

decision: Provide a network-free deterministic demo mode and a separately enabled live mode; persist and display the mode so test data or inference cannot be presented as live results.
why: The Demo must be reproducible without secrets while still supporting verifiable real-source and remote-model integration when the user configures them.

decision: Finish and validate the deterministic local runtime before live integrations, then complete the three business loops, dashboard, container validation, and documentation without using real personal data or secrets.
why: This is the safest reproducible route to the full requested Demo and preserves the explicit demo/live boundary.

decision: Keep real frontend/API operation, deterministic demo evidence, live public-read evidence, and privacy evidence distinct; fixed data or framework presence cannot substitute for live job-source validation.
why: This makes completion measurable and prevents technical implementation from overstating or changing the user's requested internet job-discovery capability.

decision: Prefer a company public ATS/Job Board GET API, beginning with a Lever Postings adapter, before best-effort JobSpy scraping. Keep every application POST endpoint outside current authorization.
why: The pinned JobSpy package exposes only LinkedIn, Indeed, and ZipRecruiter and the tested sources returned 403/451; Lever documents a public, stable-ID, read-only JSON path without changing the product goal.

decision: Label target architecture decomposition separately from the actual v0.5 graph nodes; only goal checklist evidence and implementation records establish completion.
why: The architecture document intentionally decomposes more nodes and recovery behaviors than the current code, and design presence must not be reported as implementation.

decision: Finish read-only public-source, unresolved-location, provider-failure, schema-safety, and retry evidence now; defer only real remote-model authorization, target company/location preferences, tag, and public push to the user.
why: These engineering gaps can be completed with public or fictional data and no external writes, directly following the user's instruction to accumulate only genuine decisions.

decision: Retry only failed Graph runs by resuming the same persisted LangGraph thread with null input, retain safe failure history, and reject any retry after success with HTTP 409.
why: This demonstrates actual durable execution while keeping the original run_id consistent and preventing duplicate business writes.

decision: Treat a real remote-model call as an optional, separately authorized validation rather than a mandatory local Demo freeze gate; retain the Provider gateway, outbound policy, schema validation, audit contract, and explicit demo/live labeling.
why: The user authorized controlled remote AI as a capability but prioritized a local-first runnable Demo and explicitly deferred model choices; permission to extend cannot be converted into a new mandatory completion requirement.
supersedes: The v0.6 completion classification that required one real remote-model call before Demo freeze.

decision: Implement the v0.8 job radar as a separate Tauri 2 resizable always-on-top window using the existing React/Vite frontend, MapLibre GL JS, local PMTiles, Protomaps Basemaps, a MapLibre GeoJSON/circle signal layer, and a CSS scan overlay; do not use external map tiles for the home viewport.
why: This is the smallest reusable stack that satisfies street-level styling, animated job signals, local/offline address privacy, single-file map distribution, and native floating-window behavior while preserving the existing Jobs list and three workflow boundaries.
supersedes: O-001 left the final radar/map visual direction unlocked.

decision: Use a single bundled Tauri 2 window for /radar with explicit core window permissions, persist only logical size and position in a local geometry file, and keep the API/map data on configured localhost endpoints; do not embed the API, real coordinates, transparent-window privileges or external navigation in the native host.
why: This completes the requested floating-window behavior while keeping personal data in the existing local service boundary and minimizing native permissions and persisted state.

decision: Commit the already jointly verified Phase 7.1 through 7.3 radar implementation, tests, documentation and governance provenance as one coherent local checkpoint rather than retroactively splitting the six-day-old worktree into synthetic commits.
why: The phases share a scene contract, dependency lock, privacy evidence and final native acceptance state; a single truthful checkpoint preserves provenance and rollback clarity without rewriting history.
impact_scope: current uncommitted Goal v0.8 Phase 7 worktree

decision: Add unibest/uni-app as an independent Vue 3 multi-end shell under apps/miniworld-shell while retaining the verified React/Vite dashboard and Tauri radar as existing modules; verify Web now and defer WeChat Mini Program and Android packaging.
why: The user selected unibest for the new framework and explicitly deferred WeChat construction. A separate shell preserves existing React assets and business-loop boundaries while establishing a future Web, App and Mini Program entry point.
impact_scope: system navigation and future module integration

decision: Implement Fitness as an independent uni-app module using the existing local FastAPI/PostgreSQL service as source of truth; use only a small cross-platform local draft cache for unsaved current inputs, and do not couple Fitness to Jobs, Profile/Resume, or Work Reporting.
why: The requested Web, mobile Web, Android and future Mini Program clients must share workout history, while the existing shell and backend already provide the appropriate local-only cross-end boundary. Browser storage alone cannot satisfy persistence across clients.

decision: Present Fitness body parts without sequence numbers; use whole-card short tap for entry and a 350ms long press for drag sorting on the home page; persist the resulting preference through the existing plan-order API; remove only plan-order arrows from settings while retaining exercise-order controls.
why: The user stated body parts are freely selectable rather than a prescribed sequence and explicitly chose whole-card long-press sorting plus a management page focused on editing rather than plan ordering.

decision: Extract only repeated stable Fitness presentation contracts: page shell and heading, section heading, exercise defaults fields, exercise and workout-set rows, choice chips, and settings editor rows. Keep single-use calendar, history-session detail and home-date composition page-local; keep API and workflow orchestration in pages/store.
why: This removes meaningful duplication and makes labels and controls independently testable without introducing generic wrappers for every view or moving data mutations into presentational components.

decision: Allow arbitrary switching among exercises in one active Fitness plan, persist a per-exercise 1/2/2.5/5 kg weight step, retain retry request IDs in per-exercise drafts, and derive a shared four-state workout banner from existing active-session and history data.
why: The user explicitly approved the complete T-031 plan to support real alternating workout behavior, faster weight entry and clearer workout-state feedback without changing Set history or the single Active Session rule.
impact_scope: Fitness H5 module, components and seven pages

decision: Use lime-echart 2.0.7 with Apache ECharts 5.4.3 for Fitness action trends; expose set-level and day-average modes with line/bar presentation and inside time zoom, while keeping completed PostgreSQL records as the only source of truth.
why: The user approved starting integration after component research and requested chronological history, day averaging, and a stock-chart-like time interaction without introducing a chart dependency that changes existing module boundaries.
impact_scope: Fitness stats page and chart component
third-party notices and frontend dependency lock

decision: Make goal/frontend-presentation-rules.md a mandatory completion gate; standardize mobile presentation on unibest plus Wot UI 2 and PC presentation on existing React/Vite plus Ant Design or selected ProComponents, prohibit new page-level generic UI primitives, and require physical-device evidence for applicable mobile releases.
why: The user identified repeated presentation rework as unacceptable and explicitly required the agreed component, template, responsive, state and acceptance rules to become a hard reference for all future development.
impact_scope: all current and future mobile/PC frontend tasks

decision: Adopt a calm training-console aesthetic built from Wot UI 2.3.2: warm neutral surfaces, ink text, restrained mineral green for active/primary state, compact data-led hierarchy, one primary action per screen, and system typography governed by semantic tokens.
why: The new hard rules require a mature component system and the user asked to stop repeated ad-hoc visual fixes. A task-first training console fits fast one-handed gym use while preserving readability, accessibility and the existing local-only workflow.

decision: Pin @wot-ui/ui 2.3.2 and keep runtime component resolution through the official resolver; exclude the generated Wot global component declaration from vue-tsc and use a local declaration for the Wot components used by Fitness because upstream ButtonOpenType includes an incompatible getRealtimePhoneNumber value under the current uni type set.
why: This preserves the requested mature mobile component system and H5 runtime while avoiding node_modules patches or broad type suppression. App and Mini Program compatibility remains a separate acceptance item.

decision: Implement Fitness Coach as an independent non-conversational server-side LangGraph that may reuse the platform runtime, Provider Gateway, PostgreSQL checkpointing and audit infrastructure while only reading Fitness data and only writing Agent runs and structured recommendations. Configure DeepSeek deepseek-chat as the first provider; absence of a key must yield awaiting_configuration rather than synthetic advice.
why: The user clarified that the earlier isolation requirement prohibits business-data and Graph-context coupling with Jobs, Profile/Resume and Work, not reuse of shared Agent infrastructure, and explicitly selected DeepSeek deepseek-chat for the first deployable provider entry.
